passage: I'm Zoya, and I share a desk with Dhruv, so I hear his mentoring calls. On Thursday Maria asked about switching into data journalism, and Dhruv said, 'That's outside what I know, I'd only be guessing.' I noticed he didn't leave it there. He picked up his phone, messaged a friend who works at a news desk, and wrote, 'My mentee Maria is thinking about your line of work. Could you give her twenty minutes?' Then he told Maria the friend's name and said he'd check in after the chat. Maria looked surprised, maybe a little nervous, and copied the name into her notes. A week later Maria mentioned that the friend had also introduced her to a reporter who ran a small open data project.

qa.q: What did Dhruv say when Maria asked about data journalism?
qa.a: Dhruv said, 'That's outside what I know, I'd only be guessing.'

qa.q: What might Maria have been feeling when Dhruv passed on the friend's name?
qa.a: Maria seemed surprised and maybe a little nervous, as Zoya notes, though Maria may also have felt grateful.

qa.q: What could Dhruv add to help Maria use the twenty minutes well?
qa.a: Dhruv could ask Maria to prepare two questions beforehand, so the short chat with the friend is spent on what matters most to her.

qa.q: How might Dhruv's friend at the news desk see the request?
qa.a: The friend probably sees a colleague who trusts them and may be glad to help, since twenty minutes is a modest ask.

grounding: Shows a mentor who, faced with a question outside their area, introduces the mentee to a friend in that field.

passage:
Monday. At their weekly chat, Noor asks Suraj how to move from testing into UX design. Suraj thinks, then says honestly, 'That's not my field. I'd be guessing. But I know someone who knows.'
Wednesday. Suraj sends a short message to his friend Pallavi, a UX designer at another company: 'My mentee Noor is exploring UX. Would you have twenty minutes for a call? No pressure.' Pallavi says yes. Suraj introduces them in one email with a line about each.
Two Saturdays later. Noor reports back at their chat, bright-eyed. Pallavi reviewed her sample case study, suggested an online course and invited her to a local design meetup. 'I met five designers there,' Noor says. Suraj grins. 'Now you've got more mentors than I have.'

qa.q: What did Pallavi suggest after reviewing the case study?
qa.a: An online course, plus an invitation to a local design meetup.

qa.q: How did Noor feel when reporting back?
qa.a: Noor was excited and encouraged, bright-eyed after meeting five designers.

qa.q: Why was Suraj's honesty about UX a good choice?
qa.a: Admitting it wasn't his field let him connect Noor with someone who knew, instead of giving guesses.

qa.q: How might Pallavi see being introduced?
qa.a: Pallavi got a clear, low-pressure request and may enjoy helping someone keen to enter the field.

grounding: It shows a mentor introducing the mentee to a friend in another field when a question falls outside the mentor's area, widening the mentee's network.

subtype: Approach: connecting the mentee to other people [Action]
passage: Keerthana, you asked how I ended up in climate data when I trained as a web developer. Your Divyansh sir will tell you. At twenty-four, I asked my mentor, Mrs Rao, about working on climate projects. She could have made something up. Instead she said, 'I know nothing about that world. But my college friend at the weather institute does.' That same evening she emailed him: two lines about me, two about why she thought we should talk. He met me for tea the next week. He introduced me to two researchers, one of whom later hired me. Mrs Rao never taught me a single thing about climate. What she gave me was a door to the right people. So when your mentee asks something outside your field, don't guess. Open a door.

qa.q: Where did Mrs Rao's college friend work?
How might Divyansh have felt when Mrs Rao said she knew nothing about that world?
qa.a: He may have felt surprised, even disappointed for a moment, then grateful when she made the connection that same evening.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Divyansh's story?
qa.a: Mrs Rao emailing her friend at the weather institute that evening, which led to tea, two researchers and a job.

qa.q: How might Mrs Rao's friend have seen the introduction?
qa.a: He got a short, clear email from a trusted friend, which made it easy and pleasant to agree to meet.

grounding: It shows a mentor, facing a question outside her area, introducing the mentee to a friend in that field, widening the mentee's network.
